Proper grown-up conversation and someone else cooking. Though knowing Gemma, “grown-up conversation” will involve detailed recounts of the latest drama at the school gates. Speaker_1: It probably will. She’s… invested. But it'll be good. It feels like ages since we just properly chilled. How’s Ben coping with you being out? That’s fantastic. She's always been a bit of a history buff. She told me once we were related to pirates. I think she just makes it up as she goes along. Speaker_1: Probably. I’ve been pinning ideas on Pinterest for weeks, pretending it’s for *my* non-existent parties. Speaker_1: You’re a lifesaver. Seriously. I'll make a list and we can go shopping next week. Right, Leo’s decided he wants feeding again. Duty calls.

Speaker_1: Honestly, the queues at Stansted were *insane* last month. I nearly missed my flight to Amsterdam. Speaker_2: Oh, really? I went through Gatwick - it wasn’t too bad, surprisingly. Though they were grilling everyone about their return ticket, you know, just to prove you weren’t planning on overstaying. Felt a bit…much. Speaker_1: Exactly! It's just different now, isn’t it? Can’t believe how easy it was then. Just hop on a train, no questions asked. Speaker_2: God, that was brilliant. Remember getting completely lost in Prague? We ended up in some tiny pub, filled with locals, and nobody spoke a word of English. Speaker_1: (Laughing) Oh, I remember! You tried to order a beer, and pointed frantically at someone else’s pint. I was talking to my mam about it, and she was saying it's nothing like her trips to Spain in the 70s. Speaker_2: No chance. Getting a coach to Paris used to be cheaper than a train to London. Now it feels like they’re trying to price people *out* of travelling. Speaker_2: It’s a shame, really. Those spontaneous trips were the best. Discovering hidden little towns, meeting random people… You can't really plan for that, can you? You need that freedom to just *go*. Speaker_1: You can't. I’m thinking of maybe just sticking to the UK for my holidays this year. A bit boring, but at least it’ll be stress-free. Maybe a caravan trip to the Lake District? Speaker_2: (Smiling) Now *that* sounds like a plan. Fewer passport stamps, but definitely more peace and quiet. Plus, you can’t beat a proper cuppa in a slightly damp caravan, can you? Speaker_1: Absolutely not. It's the little things, isn’t it? And less queuing. Definitely less queuing. Another pint? Speaker_2: Don't mind if I do. Speaker_1: Right, so, dessert options. We’ve got apple crumble, chocolate brownies, or… I could whip up a trifle? Speaker_2: Trifle! Trifle’s the best! With the jelly and the cream and the strawberries! Speaker_3: (Grumbling) Brownies are better. Chocolate is *always* better. Speaker_1: Okay, okay, we’ll vote. Two for trifle, one for brownies. Trifle it is then. Though you, young man, are getting extra vegetables with your dinner to balance out all that chocolate craving. Speaker_3: Aw, Mum! That’s not fair! Speaker_1: Life isn’t fair, darling. Now, who wants to set up Monopoly? Speaker_2: Me! Me! I want to be the thimble! Speaker_3: No way! I called dibs on the dog last time, you always get the thimble! Speaker_1: Right, let’s not start a war over playing pieces. You can be the car, and your sister can have the thimble. Happy? Speaker_2: Yes! Speaker_3: Fine. But I’m getting all the hotels this time. Speaker_1: That’s the spirit! Now, let’s remember the rules. No cheating, no arguing over rent, and no deliberately bankrupting each other… too quickly. Speaker_2: What does ‘bankrupting’ mean? Speaker_1: It means… when someone runs out of money and can’t pay what they owe, they have to leave the game. Speaker_3: Oh. So, like, when someone lands on my Park Lane with a hotel and they have to give me *everything*? Speaker_1: Exactly. And that’s why it's important to manage your money wisely. Don't just buy up all the properties immediately, think about building strategically… Speaker_2: Can I buy Mayfair? It's pink! Pink is my favourite! Speaker_1: You can definitely try, darling. But someone else might want it too. It all comes down to the dice and a bit of luck. And maybe some clever trading. Speaker_3: I’m saving all my money for the orange ones. They're the best ones to build on. Everyone lands on those. Speaker_1: Smart thinking. Now, let's get this game started before I change my mind and decide we're all doing spelling practice instead. Speaker_2: Noooo! Monopoly is much better! Speaker_3: Yeah! Monopoly! Speaker_1: Alright, alright. Here we go. Bank’s open… and may the best player win! Speaker_2: I *will* win! (rolls the dice with enthusiasm) Yes! Six! Speaker_3: (rolls dice) Ugh. Two. Boo. Speaker_1: (Smiling) It's going to be a long evening, isn’t it? Speaker_2: It’s going to be *fun*! Speaker_3: Not if she keeps getting lucky! Speaker_1: (Chuckles) We'll see about that. Let's play! Speaker_2: Can I buy Old Kent Road? Please? It’s only sixty pounds! Speaker_3: Don’t bother, it’s a terrible property. Speaker_1: It’s a good starting point, sweetheart. Go for it. It’s all about building an empire, remember? Speaker_2: Yes! I'm building an empire! Speaker_3: Hmph. I'll show *her* an empire. Speaker_1: (To herself, quietly) This could be a very noisy evening.

Speaker_1: Honestly, the traffic was *mental* getting out of Durham. I thought I was going to be stuck there forever. Did you see that van trying to merge onto the A1? Absolutely bonkers. Speaker_2: No, thankfully I was lost in thought. Probably contemplating the existential dread of another week at work. Though, to be fair, the A1 is always a gamble, isn't it? It’s like a slow-motion car crash waiting to happen. Speaker_1: It is. And the people who just…stop. Like, mid-lane. No warning, no indication. Just…brake. What is *that* about? Speaker_2: Probably looking at their phones. It’s the only logical explanation. People are utterly glued to those things, it’s frightening. I saw someone actually *reading* a book on the motorway the other day. A physical book! Speaker_1: No way! Seriously? That’s…a new level of recklessness. I mean, I listen to podcasts, which isn’t ideal, but at least my hands are on the wheel. A book?! Speaker_2: Swear on it. Nearly caused a pile-up. Anyway, enough complaining about terrible drivers. How was your weekend? Did you manage to get any of that corpus work done? Speaker_1: (sighs) A little. I’m so behind. Professor Davies is breathing down my neck about the metadata tagging. Apparently, I'm "not prioritising sufficiently." Like, I have a life, you know? It's not all 15th-century manuscripts and databases. Speaker_2: Sounds stressful. Academia will do that to you, eh? All those deadlines and passionate academics. I’m wrestling with a particularly stubborn drainage issue at the moment. It’s a new build, and they’ve completely botched the stormwater management. It's a headache. Speaker_1: Oh, that sounds…fun. Not. What kind of botched? Like, flooding kind of botched? Speaker_2: Potentially. If we get another downpour like last week, yes. It’s all very politically sensitive, obviously. The developers don't want to admit fault, the local council is breathing down *my* neck…it's a whole thing. It’s just…engineering, you know? It should be straightforward. It *should* work. Speaker_1: Right? You'd think something as basic as drainage... It's like when the washing machine breaks and you just want someone to fix it, not explain the complex mechanics of the impeller. Speaker_2: Precisely! I just want it to *not leak*! Is that too much to ask? Speaker_1: Apparently. Speaker_2: So, Durham aside, how’s family? Has your grandma been keeping busy with her knitting? Speaker_1: Oh aye, she's always knitting. She’s started on a blanket for my cousin’s new baby. It’s going to be massive. She’s determined it’ll be big enough to cover the whole living room. Speaker_2: (laughs) That sounds like your grandma. She's a force of nature. Speaker_1: She is. A very crafty, knitting-obsessed force of nature. Speaker_2: Good. Always good to have a crafty force of nature in the family. Speaker_1: Definitely. Speaker_2: Right. Only… seventy miles to go. Brace yourself for more A1 adventures. Speaker_1: Oh joy. Speaker_1: May the traffic gods be with us. Speaker_2: Amen to that. Speaker_2: Do you want me to put some music on?

Speaker_1: Right then, finished the crossword. Took me ages with 23 down, "Maritime mammal, six letters". Thought it was a whale at first, but the crossing letters didn’t fit. Turns out it was a seal. Speaker_2: A seal, eh? I never could get on with those crosswords. Too much thinking. Give me a good detective novel any day. Something with a proper twist. Not these modern ones where it's obvious who did it halfway through. Speaker_3: Oh, I used to enjoy a good crossword. Keeps the brain ticking, you know. Though I haven't done one in… well, a good while now. Since Arthur's been less mobile, I’ve been spending more time just sitting with him, really. Speaker_1: Understandable, love. It's good of you, it is. He's a lucky man. Did you see young Kevin down the road? New car, bright red. Showed off something awful when he drove past this morning. Speaker_2: Kevin? The one who used to leave his motorbike engine running outside our house at seven in the morning? Good riddance to bad rubbish, I say. A fancy car won’t change his manners. Speaker_3: Now, now, Arthur. That's a bit harsh. He's just a young lad trying to get on. Though I agree, the noise *was* dreadful. Reminded me of your motorbike days, though, didn't it? Roaring around the countryside. Speaker_1: (Chuckles) Those were the days, eh? Before speed cameras and health and safety. Good times. Still, at least Kevin's got a job to pay for it. Seems hard to come by these days, decent work. Speaker_2: They all seem to be working in warehouses now, boxed up like sardines. No pride in their work, none at all. Used to be, you learned a trade. Bricklaying, carpentry, something you could *do* with your hands. Speaker_3: My brother, George, he was a brilliant carpenter. Could build anything. Made a lovely rocking horse for little Emily when she was born. Still got it, up in the attic. Speaker_1: Emily’s grown now, isn't she? Doesn't seem five minutes ago she was a little 'un climbing all over us. Time flies, doesn't it? Speaker_2: Flies like a greased whippet. Remember when we used to take her to the beach at Cromer? Building sandcastles until her little hands were raw? Speaker_3: And she’d always insist on wearing those bright pink wellies, even on sunny days! She was a determined one, that girl. Speaker_1: She is. Good girl. Speaking of the beach, a bit chilly for a walk later, wouldn't you say? Speaker_2: Chilly? It’s Norfolk, it’s *always* chilly. Still, a bit of fresh air wouldn't go amiss. Keeps you awake. Speaker_3: I think I'll just sit here with a cup of tea, if you don't mind. My knees are playing up a bit today. Speaker_1: Of course, love. I'll put the kettle on then. More biscuits, Arthur? Speaker_2: Don't mind if I do. Custard creams, if you have them. Can’t beat a custard cream. speaker_1: They never should have got rid of the custard creams. Speaker_3: They've brought them back, haven’t they? Speaker_1:Have they? When. Speaker_2: Oh about six months ago. I told you. Speaker_1: No you didn't. Speaker_2: Yes I did. Speaker_3: Oh, leave him, Arthur. He forgets everything these days. Speaker_1: I do not!

Speaker_1: Right, so I was thinking about the packaging, and I genuinely think we need to step it up. The jars are…fine, but they just feel a bit, well, cheap. Especially when we’re positioning ourselves as a natural, premium brand. Speaker_2: Yeah, I get that. It's hard though, isn’t it? Because the frosted glass ones, the ones I showed you, are nearly triple the price per unit. That really eats into the profit margin, especially when we’re trying to keep everything affordable. Speaker_1: I know, I know. It's a balance. But think about it – people *judge* a book by its cover. And skincare, even more so. It’s a visual product. They see it on Instagram, they see it in someone’s bathroom, it needs to *look* expensive, even if it's not astronomically priced. What about a compromise? Maybe slightly thicker glass? And we could look at a different lid – something rose gold, maybe? Speaker_2: Rose gold… hmm. Potentially? I’m a bit worried about trends, though. Rose gold feels a bit…last year, doesn't it? Would silver be better? More timeless? Speaker_1: Hmm, good point. Silver is safer. Okay, silver lids. But definitely thicker glass. And we need to get the dimensions right. I’ve been trying to visualise it with the labels, and I’m worried the current jars look a bit squat. Speaker_2: Squat? What do you mean? Speaker_1: Just…not elegant. I was looking at some competitor packaging online, and theirs are taller, more streamlined. I have some measurements here, actually. Their standard jar is 70mm in diameter and 85mm high. Ours are 65mm diameter and 75mm high. It’s not a massive difference, but it could make a big impact. Speaker_2: Okay, that’s helpful. I can send those specs to the supplier, see how much of a price difference it makes. It might be worth getting a sample made, just to compare. Speaking of suppliers, I finally managed to get hold of Mark - he's been swamped. He's confirmed the organic rosehip oil order, which is brilliant. It’s arriving next week. Speaker_1: Oh, fantastic! That’s a relief. We were getting low. I’ve been meaning to ask, how’s the Etsy shop doing? Have you seen a boost since that influencer posted about us? Speaker_2: It was crazy for about 48 hours. We completely sold out of the face balm! I've been frantically making more. It’s started to calm down now, but overall, sales are up about 30% since then. It’s insane. I think I need to start looking at maybe getting some help with fulfillment. It's taking over my evenings. Speaker_1: That’s amazing though! 30% is huge. You’re doing really well. Maybe your cousin Liam? He was looking for something to do after he finished college, wasn't he? Speaker_2: Maybe. He's a bit flaky, to be honest. But it’s worth asking. Speaking of flaky, Mum keeps asking when we’re going to take her to the coast for a weekend. She's convinced Honest Skincare is going to make us millionaires and she wants a beachside hotel. Speaker_1: (Laughing) Oh, bless her. She's so optimistic. We're a long way off a beachside hotel, but it’s nice she’s rooting for us. Maybe we can squeeze in a day trip to Brighton in August? If we don’t have too many orders to fulfill. Speaker_2: That sounds good. I'm already stressing about August, to be honest, it’s our busiest time normally. But hey, at least we have good problems to have, right? And maybe, just maybe, Mum will get her seaside wish.

Speaker_1: Honestly, the price of everything is just… scandalous now, isn’t it? I went to get a loaf of bread yesterday – a *loaf* – and nearly choked. Three pounds! Three pounds for a basic white loaf. Speaker_2: You’re telling me! I filled the car up this morning. Nearly a hundred quid. A hundred! Used to be able to do it for sixty, comfortably. They say it’s the global situation, but it feels like they’re just taking the mickey. Speaker_1: Aye, that’s what I think. Taking advantage, the lot of them. Did you see that piece on the news about the water companies? Pumping sewage into the sea! Utterly disgraceful. Speaker_2: I did. Shocking. And they’re still getting away with it. Bonuses for the executives, while everyone else is struggling to pay their bills. Makes you wonder where it'll all end. Speaker_1: It does indeed. Though, to be fair, I’m mostly worried about the heating. I’ve been trying to be sensible, keeping the thermostat down, wearing layers… but it’s still going to be a hefty bill this winter. Speaker_2: You’re better off than some, at least you’ve got a decent house. Old Man Hemmings next door is practically living in a tent in his living room, he says, just to save a few pounds. Speaker_1: Oh, the poor man. I must pop round with a tin of biscuits, he always appreciates a bit of shortbread. How are things with you and Margaret? Still planning that trip to Cornwall? Speaker_2: We are, yes. Booked the cottage for a week in October. Hopefully, the weather will be kind. Margaret’s been a bit… anxious about it lately. Speaker_1: Oh? What’s the matter? Speaker_2: Her sister, Brenda, isn't well. Not serious, thankfully, but she's got some sort of chest infection. Margaret’s worried about leaving her on her own, you see. Brenda lives alone and… well, she’s not the most self-sufficient. Speaker_1: Oh, dear. That’s a worry. Is there anyone else who can help Brenda out while you’re away? Her son, perhaps? Speaker_2: He’s offered to pop in, but he lives up in Manchester. It’s a long drive for just a quick check-in. Margaret was thinking of asking Mrs. Davies, you know, from down the road. She's always been very kind to Brenda. Speaker_1: Mrs. Davies is a good soul. She'd be happy to help, I'm sure. It’s good of Margaret to worry, though. That's just her nature. Always thinking of others. Speaker_2: It is. Sometimes, I think she worries *too* much. But that’s Margaret, isn’t it? Makes me appreciate her all the more, though. Keeps me grounded. Speaker_1: Aye, she's a good woman. And you’re a lucky man, John. Don't forget that. Now, are you having tea? I’ve just made a fresh pot. I’ve got some of those lemon biscuits you like. Speaker_2: Lemon biscuits? You read my mind! Tea would be lovely, thank you, sis. It’s good to have a proper chat, you know? Sometimes, it just helps to vent. Speaker_1: That’s what sisters are for, John. That’s what we’re here for. Now, sit yourself down and tell me all about this car bill…

Speaker_1: Honestly, this weather is ridiculous for November. It feels like… April. Speaker_2: Tell me about it. I was wearing a t-shirt walking the dog this morning. The dog was looking at me like *I* was the weird one. Speaker_3: It's unsettling, isn't it? My mum keeps moaning that the birds haven't started nesting properly. She’s convinced it’s a sign of the apocalypse. Speaker_4: (Chuckles) Your mum’s a character. Still, she’s probably not entirely wrong. Nature’s usually a pretty good indicator. Though, frankly, I’m not complaining about being able to work in the shed without needing three layers. Speaker_1: Speaking of the shed, are you still battling with that router table? You were muttering about it last time we saw you. Speaker_4: Oh, don’t even get me started. It’s a temperamental beast. I think the fence is slightly off, and I can’t seem to get it perfectly aligned. It’s driving me mental. I’m starting to think I should just sell it and go back to hand-planing. Speaker_2: Sounds stressful. Remind me to steer clear of any requests for bespoke furniture then. Speaker_3: You’re always so productive though. I’m struggling to even *think* about Christmas presents. I feel so behind. Have you started planning, Amy? Speaker_1: A little. Primarily focusing on food. I’m thinking a full roast this year – turkey, all the trimmings. I'm trying to get ahead and order everything online. Trying to avoid the supermarket chaos, you know? Speaker_4: Good plan. I’ve learned my lesson trying to leave it to the last minute. Remember that year I tried to get a goose? Ended up with a frozen chicken because all the geese were gone! Speaker_2: (Laughing) Oh god, yes! The Great Goose Hunt of 2018. Speaker_3: Sounds traumatic. I’m thinking of doing a vegetarian feast. My sister's converted, and it makes things slightly less complicated. Speaker_1: That sounds lovely. It’s nice to mix it up. We're having… well, my dad’s already starting to talk about his retirement plan. It involves moving to Spain and spending his days picking mulberries. Speaker_2: Mulberries? Speaker_1: Apparently, they’re a superfood! He’s read something online. Keeps going on about the ‘Mediterranean diet’. He’ll be sunburnt and complaining within a week, I guarantee it. Speaker_3: (Smiling) Bless him. He’s always been a bit of a dreamer. Speaker_4: Is he any good at DIY? Because if he *is*, Spain might not be ready. Speaker_1: (Scoffs) Don’t even ask. He once tried to fix a leaky tap with duct tape and a rubber band. It ended in a small flood. Speaker_2: Right, so, definitely no DIY in Spain then. Has anyone got any good game recommendations? We're thinking of having a games night after Christmas dinner to avoid family arguments. Speaker_3: Codenames is always a hit. Or Carcassonne if you want something a bit more strategic. Speaker_4: I’m rather partial to Ticket to Ride. It’s… mildly competitive. Usually ends up with someone accusing me of hoarding train cards. Speaker_1: We've got a new one, Azul. It's pretty, and surprisingly addictive. It’s all about tiling patterns. Very calming, allegedly. Though I suspect it will descend into chaos eventually. Speaker_2: Sounds good. Oh, and I nearly forgot – I've managed to snag tickets to that winter light festival in Cardiff. Anyone fancy joining me in January?

Speaker_1: Honestly, this cutlery is dreadful. It’s like eating with plastic spoons. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Bit harsh, isn't it? It's just…normal cutlery. Mum’s always had pretty basic stuff. Speaker_3: Now, now, don’t be like that, love. It gets the job done, doesn’t it? It’s clean, and it holds your food. What more do you want? Speaker_4: She’s got a point, you know. It’s perfectly serviceable. Though, I do recall your grandmother having silver. Proper silver. Polish it ‘til your arm aches, that stuff. Speaker_1: I just… I keep bending the forks. It’s embarrassing when you're trying to get the last bit of potato. Speaker_5: Aye, forks bendin’. Used to happen all the time wi’ the cheap stuff we had. Me dad, he’d just straighten ‘em out wi’ pliers. Not very elegant, mind. Speaker_2: Pliers? Really? Speaker_5: Aye. Resourceful, he was. Couldn’t afford new ones every time one got a little bent. Times were different then, you see. Speaker_3: He sounds like my father. "Make do and mend" was his motto. I remember him patching up my brother’s trousers with bits of old flour sacks. Speaker_1: (Smiling slightly) Oh, bless. Speaking of patching things up, how's the leak in the roof going, Mum? Speaker_3: Oh, don’t even ask. The man came round, had a look, said it’s worse than he thought. Needs more than just a patch, apparently. Wants to replace a whole section. Speaker_4: Oh, dear. That sounds expensive. Speaker_3: You have no idea. I’m waiting for a quote. Probably going to have to raid my savings. Speaker_2: That’s rough. Maybe I could help out a bit? I’ve got a little saved from my bonus. Speaker_3: Oh, that’s very kind, love, but I couldn’t possibly. You need that for yourself. Speaker_1: No, honestly, Mum, let us help. It’s your house, and we want you to be comfortable. Speaker_4: They’re right, you know. Don't be proud. Family helps each other. Speaker_5: Aye. That's what family’s for. Offering a hand when someone's down. Don't let her struggle on her own. Speaker_3: (Sighs) Alright, alright. If you insist. But I swear, I’ll pay you back as soon as I can. Speaker_2: Don’t worry about it, Mum. It’s not a loan. Speaker_1: How was Sarah’s hen do, by the way? Did you have a good time? Speaker_3: Oh, it was chaos! She insisted on karaoke. Honestly, the noise… and the outfits! Bright pink feather boas everywhere. Speaker_4: (Laughing) Sounds lively. Sarah always did like a bit of attention. Speaker_3: She does. And she’s marrying a good lad. Quite quiet, but a good lad. Remember Mark? From university? Speaker_1: Vaguely. Tall, bit shy? Speaker_3: That’s the one. They’re planning a small wedding, just close family and friends. Down in Devon, I think. Speaker_2: Devon’s nice. I went there on holiday once. Lovely beaches. Speaker_5: I remember Devon. Went there as a lad, with me parents. Didn't have much money back then, but we had a good time. Simple pleasures, you know? Buildin’ sandcastles, paddlin’ in the sea… Speaker_1: Sounds idyllic. I need a holiday. Somewhere with nice cutlery, preferably. And a roof that doesn’t leak.

Speaker_1: Honestly, the meeting was dreadful. Just… endless spreadsheets and people arguing about percentages. You wouldn't believe it. Speaker_2: (Mouth full of food) Mmm hmm. Are we still going skiing? Speaker_1: Of course, we're still going skiing! I just announced that to the entire office, actually. Used it as a threat to get them to finish their reports. “If these aren’t on my desk by Friday, I’m taking a week off to go skiing!” Speaker_2: Good! Can I take my sparkly skis? The pink ones? Speaker_1: The pink ones? Darling, you’ve barely used those. They’re practically brand new. And remember what happened last time? You kept complaining they were too… sparkly. Speaker_2: They *were* too sparkly. They made my eyes hurt. But I still want to bring them. Just in case. Speaker_1: We’ll talk about the skis later. Have you finished your peas? I’m worried about you being good on the slopes if you don’t eat your greens. You need your energy. Speaker_2: They're yucky. Can I have more bread instead? Speaker_1: Just a few more peas, please. Dominated Wimbledon for years before Federer came along. Speaker_3: He was a bit of a showman too, wasn’t he? Threw his racket around a bit. Not like the controlled aggression of Djokovic or Alcaraz. I’ve put the potatoes on too, so dinner will be ready soon. Speaker_2: Okay. Can I go and check my phone then? Speaker_3: In a bit. Finish talking about tennis first. It’s good to talk about your progress. It shows you're thinking about it. And maybe, just maybe, you’ll become the next Alcaraz. Speaker_2: (grumbling) Doubt it. Speaker_1: Don’t be so negative! Just give it your best shot. That's all we ask. Speaker_3: Exactly. And then you can tell us all about it over dinner. Speaker_2: Fine. But if I lose, don’t say “I told you so”.

Speaker_1: These napkins… seriously? They look like… underpants. Speaker_2: (Laughing) Oh, don’t be daft, Liam! They’re festive! Little snowflakes! Speaker_3: They *do* kind of resemble a pair of briefs, though. Especially when you fold them. Speaker_4: Your mum got them in the sale, didn't she, love? Speaker_2: Your dad did a fantastic job. Though he nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to baste it. Speaker_4: Nearly. A little smoky. But we averted disaster. Mostly just people wearing Christmas jumpers with shorts. Speaker_5: That sounds… odd. Still, at least you had a break from the weather. This has been a dreadful December. Non-stop rain. Still gets me every time. Speaker_1: That’s so old! Speaker_2: It’s a classic! And the music is beautiful. Do you remember when they had that ballroom scene, and… Speaker_3: Mum, we’ve had this conversation. Speaker_4: (Chuckling) Leave her alone. She’s a *Downton Abbey* devotee. Speaker_5: You know, I used to play the piano. Not very well, mind you. But I loved it. Your grandma encouraged me. Speaker_1: Did she have a piano here? Speaker_5: She did! In the front room. A beautiful mahogany one. It’s gone now, of course. Your aunt Carol has it. Speaker_4: Perhaps we should all learn an instrument. Get a family band going. Speaker_3: (Laughing) I think I'll stick to singing in the shower. Speaker_2: And what about those dance moves you were showing us earlier, Liam? Those were… something. Speaker_1: They’re the latest TikTok trend! Everyone’s doing them! Speaker_4: Well, as long as you don't try them on your grandma. She might have a heart attack!

Speaker_1: Honestly, this week has been *insane* at work. Just back-to-back meetings, everyone panicking about deadlines… It’s exhausting. Speaker_2: Oh, tell me about it. Still, it’s their money, isn’t it? Speaker_1: I suppose. It just feels a bit…flaunted, sometimes. Especially when you're scrimping and saving just to afford a basic life. Speaker_2: (Laughing) Oh, Geoff! He couldn’t drive to save his life, let alone a sports car. Nearly took out Mrs. Higgins' prize-winning roses. Speaker_1: Right, I’m just going to get the pasta on. Do you want me to do a tomato sauce or something a bit creamier? Speaker_2: Creamy sounds lovely actually, after the day I’ve had. People just don’t seem to understand they're sentient beings. It’s the same with cats, really. People think they’re aloof and independent, but they feel things deeply. Speaker_1: Absolutely. Right, sauce is simmering. I’m thinking of tackling that crossword later. That cryptic one from Saturday is proving particularly devious. Speaker_2: Ooh, good luck with that. I’ve heard really good things about that one. Speaker_2: *Trapped* sounds good. We’ve had enough zombies for one week, I think. Oh, and I found that bottle of wine in the cellar, the one we’ve had for… fourteen years? Speaker_1: (Eyes widen) The Merlot? Oh dear. I’m not sure that’s going to be very drinkable. Speaker_2: We can but try. Though I suspect it will taste like vinegar. Maybe we should just stick to the supermarket wine. Speaking of which, I need to get a new blender. Mine’s making awful noises. Sounds like a jet engine taking off. Speaker_1: Oh that’s annoying. You are a magnet for broken appliances. Speaker_2: I know. It’s a gift. Speaker_1: (Laughs) Indeed it is. Right, pasta’s nearly done, sauce is ready. Supper is served!

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’ve spent way too much money this month. Like, legitimately worried about my bank account. Speaker_2: Tell me about it! I impulse bought a dress online last night. I was scrolling through ASOS earlier and nearly bought six different pairs of boots. Six! Speaker_4: You lot are terrible. I’m trying to be good. I’m really hoping I can get away with wearing these jeans again tonight. They’re… mostly clean. Speaker_5: Mostly? What does that even *mean*? Is there a suspicious stain? What are you wearing tonight, anyway? I'm thinking the black skirt, but I can’t decide on a top. Speaker_2: I’m wearing that sparkly thing I got from Primark. It’s ridiculously over the top, but it’s a Saturday night, innit? Gotta embrace the chaos. Speaker_3: I'm going for comfy-chic. Black leggings, a nice jumper, and… probably trainers. I ended up borrowing someone else's trainers. Speaker_1: I'm attempting heels. I’ve got these new platforms, but I’ve only worn them around the house, so it’s a bit of a gamble. I'm predicting needing a piggyback by the end of the night. Speaker_2: Oh, you'll be fine. Just pace yourself with the drinks, yeah? Speaking of which… pre-drinks at mine? I’ve got some prosecco chilling. Speaker_3: Yes! Prosecco is a *must*. But not too much prosecco before we head out. We don’t want any embarrassing incidents. Remember Sarah last month? Speaker_4: Oh, *god* don't remind me. She tried to have a full-blown conversation with a lamppost. Speaker_5: It was a very serious conversation, apparently. About the importance of street lighting. What time shall we all be over? Like, sevenish? Speaker_3: Seven sounds good. Gives me enough time to wrestle myself into vaguely presentable clothing and attempt to control my online shopping urges one last time. Speaker_4: Seven works for me. I’ll try and scrub the chip shop evidence off my jeans. Speaker_5: Brilliant. This is going to be a good night, even if I do end up carrying someone home. Speaker_1: Do we think it's going to be rammed? I heard that new club is really popular. Speaker_2: Yeah, probably. But we'll stick together, yeah? No one gets left behind. Especially after the lamppost incident. Speaker_3: Definitely. Safety in numbers. And I'm having a designated dance-floor buddy, just in case I start spontaneously combusting with awkwardness. Speaker_4: I'll volunteer. I'm a professional awkwardness absorber. Speaker_5: Oh good, because I’ll need someone to stop me from attempting any questionable dance moves. They’re, like, a historical reenactment of 90s boyband routines.

Speaker_1: Honestly, I just… I don’t *get* people who are relentlessly optimistic. It’s exhausting. Like, everything’s rainbows and unicorns, even when their cat’s just died. Speaker_2: (Sipping his coffee) You think they're faking it? Speaker_1: No, not faking. Just… fundamentally different wiring. I need a bit of realism. A bit of “Oh, this is awful, isn’t it?” before leaping to solutions. It’s the constant positivity that grates. Brenda at work is like that. Drives me mad. Speaker_2: Brenda, huh? Sounds a bit… much. Remember Auntie Mavis? Similar vibe. Always talking about finding her ‘spiritual path’. Speaker_1: Oh god, yes. The crystals, the incense, the whispered pronouncements about energy fields. It was… a lot. You always handled her with such grace, though. I just wanted to roll my eyes. Speaker_2: Someone had to. But she *was* harmless. I think she genuinely believed she was on some grand spiritual journey. Made her happy, I suppose. You ever feel like that, by the way? Like you're supposed to be *searching* for something bigger? Speaker_1: Occasionally. But then I remember I just want a quiet evening and a good book and think, “No, I’m probably fine as I am." Do you believe in soulmates? Speaker_2: Honestly? I used to. Very emphatically, in my twenties. Now… I think it’s a lovely idea, but probably a bit romanticised. I’m quite happy with a very compatible and affectionate life partner. You? Speaker_1: I'm leaning towards compatible as well. The idea of one perfect person out there is a bit terrifying, actually. Too much pressure. Although, sometimes, when we’re just… being comfortable together, I do think, “Yeah, this is pretty good.” Speaker_2: See? That's better than needing a soulmate. Imagine if we’d both spent our lives looking for 'the one' and missed out on this. Speaker_1: True. It’s just… sometimes I fantasise about visiting different periods in history. Like, what would it have been like to be a flapper in the twenties? Or a Victorian lady in a huge dress? Speaker_2: (Chuckles) You’d be terrible as a Victorian lady. Too much sass. You’d have scandalised everyone. Speaker_1: Probably. Although, imagine the parties! Those grand balls, the elaborate etiquette… I’d be all over that. I’m planning an imaginary party right now. It’s 1928, everyone’s wearing sequins, there’s a jazz band…and Brenda from work is banned. Speaker_2: Harsh. But fair. I’m inviting Oscar Wilde. And possibly a dinosaur. Speaker_1: A dinosaur? Really? Speaker_2: Well, why not? It's *my* imaginary party. And I think a Brachiosaurus would add a certain je ne sais quoi. Oh, speaking of which, I promised I'd look at your mother's laptop this afternoon. She’s convinced it’s been taken over by Russians. Speaker_1: Oh, brilliant. Thank you. She’s already blaming Putin for the patchy Wi-Fi. Speaker_2: It’s always Putin. Look, I’m really sorry I was a bit grumpy yesterday. About the kitchen. I was just stressed with that project at work. Speaker_1: It’s okay. I was being a bit sensitive. I do get fiercely protective of my kitchen. It's my sanctuary. And you were right, it *was* a bit chaotic. Speaker_2: It was. Right, coffee finished. Laptop rescue mission, then. And maybe, just maybe, we can sneak in a quick game of Scrabble later? Speaker_1: Now *that* sounds like a perfect evening. Dinosaur-free, hopefully.

Speaker_1: Honestly, this new client is driving me round the bend. They want everything yesterday, and then complain when it’s not perfect first time. You wouldn’t believe the emails. Speaker_2: Oh, tell me about it. I had a bloke today who wanted me to expedite a form… which he’d only *just* submitted. Like, I physically can’t make it go faster, mate. Speaker_3: Men! Honestly. They think we have some sort of magic button. Though, actually, I had a right drama with Brenda this morning. She’s called in sick *again*. Speaker_1: Oh no, not Brenda? What’s she claiming this time? Speaker_3: Migraine. I’m starting to think she enjoys a duvet day. I mean, honestly, twice in one month? I’m not saying she’s lying, but… Speaker_2: People take the mick, don’t they? Though, a proper migraine is awful. My mum gets them. Makes her see spots. Speaker_1: True, true. Still, it messes up the admin no end. Anyway, enough about work. How’s the knitting going? Did you finish that jumper for your nephew? Speaker_2: Nearly! Just the sleeves left. It's a bit wonky, I’ll be honest. I’m not exactly a master knitter. It’s more…rustic. He’ll love it. He’s five, he doesn't care. Speaker_3: That’s sweet. I keep meaning to take it up again. It’s so relaxing. Though, I worry I’d just end up with a pile of unfinished projects. Like I do with everything. Speaking of projects, have you two seen that documentary about cemeteries? The Victorian ones, all the elaborate tombstones? Speaker_1: Oh, the one on Channel 4? Yes! It was fascinating, wasn't it? All that symbolism. And the stories behind the people. Speaker_2: I missed that. Was it good? I love graveyards, weirdly. They’re so…peaceful. And you can learn so much about history. Speaker_3: It’s amazing. Apparently, the bigger the tombstone, the more… important you were. And they used to write these incredibly long, poetic epitaphs. It’s a completely different attitude to death than we have now. Speaker_1: It is. Everything's so rushed and clinical these days. My aunt’s just had her funeral. Very simple. It felt… wrong, somehow. Not celebrating her life enough. Speaker_2: I think it depends on the person, doesn’t it? My grandad wouldn’t have wanted a fuss. Just wanted to be… gone. Speaker_3: Fair enough. Although, I do think we’ve become a bit desensitised to death. Especially with everything you see on the news. All the violence... it's terrifying. I read something the other day about gun crime in America... it's shocking. Speaker_1: It *is* terrifying. And it's creeping closer, isn't it? You see things happening even here now. It makes you worry about bringing up children. Speaker_2: It does. It's not the world we grew up in, is it? Speaking of children, are you two still trying for another one? Speaker_1: We are, yes. It’s… proving a bit difficult. We’re going to see a specialist next month. Speaker_3: Oh, darling, I’m so sorry to hear that. I’m sending you both all my love. And I’m here if you want to talk, anytime. Speaker_1: Thank you, that means a lot. It's just… frustrating. Everyone else seems to fall pregnant without trying. Speaker_3: Don’t do that to yourself! Everyone’s journey is different. Plus, you have Leo and Daisy. They’re wonderful children. And honestly, have you seen the price of childcare these days? A good reason *not* to have

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m starting to think Millie’s just…making it up. About the landlord being rubbish. Like, every week it’s something new. Speaker_2: Making it up? Really? She seemed pretty stressed when she was telling us about the leak last week. Proper soaked her trainers, she said. Speaker_3: Yeah, but then she was bragging about how she got him to agree to fix the bathroom *and* give her a discount on rent. Bit sus, innit? Speaker_1: Exactly! She's a master manipulator. I swear she enjoys the drama. Remember when she said her flatmate stole her pasta? Speaker_2: Oh god, yes! And then it turned out she’d just…misplaced it in the back of the cupboard. Classic Millie. Speaker_3: It’s exhausting being around her sometimes. Like, can’t we just have one conversation that *doesn’t* involve a crisis? Speaker_1: Tell me about it. Speaking of exhausting, has anyone sorted out their tax code thing yet? I keep getting emails from HMRC and honestly, it just looks like code to me. Speaker_2: Nah, I’m putting it off. It feels like a trap. I'm pretty sure as soon as I click anything, they’ll demand all my student loan and then some. Speaker_3: I’ve started it, but I’m already confused. Apparently, I ‘earned’ £3,000 from…existing? Is that a thing? Speaker_1: They just say that to mess with us, I reckon. It’s probably just the maintenance loan. Anyway, are we still going to the match on Saturday? I managed to snag tickets. Speaker_2: Sick! Yeah, definitely. Unless… Wait, what time is it again? I promised Jamie I’d help him with his essay. It’s about post-structuralism or something. Sounds horrific. Speaker_3: Oh dear god. Jamie and post-structuralism. That’s a recipe for disaster. He spent two hours trying to explain nihilism to me last week and I still haven’t recovered. Speaker_1: Just tell him you’re busy! The football's more important. Plus, apparently, there's a new burger van outside the stadium. They do loaded fries. Speaker_2: Loaded fries? Now *that* is a good enough reason to ditch post-structuralism. Consider Jamie ditched. Speaker_3: Good. Speaking of ditching things, I need to go to the shops later. I’m out of biscuits. Actually, no, scratch that. I'm out of *everything*. I think I survived on pesto pasta for three days straight last week. Speaker_1: You’re a minimalist. You're just living the simple life. Speaker_2: (imitating a posh voice) “Oh, the simplicity of pesto. A truly refined palate.” Speaker_3: Oh, shut up! You just pronounce "scone" like "gone." It drives me mad. Speaker_1: Oh, *here* we go... the great scone debate. Speaker_2: Look, it’s just…logical. It rhymes with “gone!” What’s not to understand? It’s phonetically sound. Speaker_3: It's not phonetically sound! It's scone, as in cone! It’s a… a biscuit! A sweet treat! It should sound sweet! Speaker_1: (laughing) Okay, okay, calm down, you two. Let's just agree to disagree and focus on the important things. Like loaded fries. And avoiding Millie’s latest crisis.

Speaker_1: This seafood risotto is *amazing*. Honestly, the best thing I’ve eaten all week. Speaker_2: (Smiling) Glad you're enjoying it, love. It's good, isn’t it? A bit different to Greggs, eh? Speaker_3: (Mouth full) Mmmph. It’s good. Can I have some of your chips, Dad? Speaker_4: (Chuckles) You’ve barely touched your own! Finish those first, then we’ll talk chips. So, Sarah, still loving university? How’s the dissertation going? Speaker_1: It's… a process. Honestly, I spend more time procrastinating on Facebook than actually writing it. I found like, five old school photos of me and Liam today. Ridiculous. Speaker_2: Facebook, honestly. It’s a time thief. I only go on to look at pictures of people’s grandchildren. And confirm I haven't missed any sudden births. Speaker_3: Gran, you always say that! Like, you just check for babies! Speaker_2: Well, someone has to, don't they? It's a demanding job, you know. Had a tricky one last week – mum came in, convinced she was in labour, turned out to be gas! Speaker_4: Sounds stressful. My days are mostly spreadsheets and powerpoint presentations, thankfully. Although, I had a client last week who wanted to redesign his entire company based on… moped culture. Speaker_1: Moped culture? What even *is* that? Speaker_4: Apparently, it’s a thing. A very niche thing. Lots of talk about vintage Vespas and artisanal helmets. Speaker_3: (Snorts) Dad, you're making that up. Speaker_4: I assure you, I am not. He wanted the office to look like a 1960s Italian scooter repair shop. Speaker_2: Oh, bless him. He sounds a bit lost. Anyway, Liam, how’s school? Any plans for the summer? Speaker_3: Just… chilling, I guess. Probably playing FIFA with Ben. Maybe get a new bike. Speaker_1: You still playing football then? You were talking about giving it up… Speaker_3: Nah, I still play. Just not as much. It’s alright. It’s getting harder with everyone getting bigger and stronger though. Speaker_4: Remember when you used to complain about the bus being late for football practice? That seems like ages ago. Speaker_1: Oh god, don’t remind me. That number 8 bus was the bane of my life. Always fifteen minutes late. Speaker_2: And the smell! It always smelled like wet dog and chips. Speaking of dogs, how's Winston doing, Hazel? He alright? Speaker_1: He's good. He's been getting a lot of walks with Emily. He’s getting a bit grey around the muzzle now, poor thing. Starting to slow down. Speaker_4: They don't stay puppies forever, do they? It’s heartbreaking. Speaker_3: Can we go get ice cream after this? Speaker_2: We’ll see. Finish your dinner first. Honestly, you eat like a bird. Speaker_1: Mum, you always say that too! Speaker_4: This wine is very good. Reminds me of that little vineyard we visited in Tuscany. Remember that, darling? Speaker_2: Of course. Lovely place. Although, I spent the whole time worrying about getting back to the hospital. Always on call, you see. Even on holiday. Speaker_1: You're a machine, Mum. Honestly. Speaker_3: Can I get an Xbox when I’m older? Like, a really good one. Speaker_4: We’ll see what happens. You need to focus on your schoolwork first. Speaker_1: Liam! Behave. And Dad, don’t encourage him! This is why we can’t have nice things.

Speaker_1: Right then, well that's the bags mostly unpacked. Didn’t half rain on the way back, did it? Thought we were bringing the Cornish weather *with* us. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) You always say that, dear. It always rains when you come back from somewhere nice. It’s a law of nature, I reckon. How did you get on with unloading everything from the car? Your back must be playing up again. Speaker_1: Managed alright. Young David next door gave me a hand with the heavier bits. Good lad, he is. Though he kept going on about this cycle race that went through the village yesterday. Said it was “massive.” Didn’t see a thing, of course, stuck in traffic most of the afternoon. Speaker_3: Oh, the Tour of Britain passed through near me too, actually. Went through Solihull. It was quite a spectacle. Loads of people lining the streets. Though I mostly saw it on the telly, let’s be honest. Easier on the knees. Speaker_2: So, Cornwall. Tell me *everything*. You were volunteering at the YHA again, weren’t you? How was that? Speaker_1: Oh, lovely. Absolutely lovely. Different bunch this time. A couple from Australia, a German student… and a rather quiet young man who just kept taking photographs. Spent hours up at the lighthouse, he did. Speaker_3: The lighthouse? Which one? St. Michael’s Mount? Speaker_1: No, the one at Godrevy. You know, the one Virginia Woolf wrote about. He was obsessed with it. Kept taking pictures of the waves crashing against it. Said it was “elemental.” Sounds a bit pretentious, doesn’t it? Speaker_2: (Smiling) Sounds artistic. He probably had a whole project dedicated to lighthouses! Did you talk to him much? Speaker_1: Not really. He was a bit stand-offish. But the others were a good laugh. We had a day trip to St Ives, and then a walk along the coast path. Got absolutely drenched, as I said. Saw some crabs though, big ones! Speaker_3: Crabs, eh? Always reminds me of holidays as a kid. Trying to catch them with a bucket and a net. Never had much luck. Speaker_2: Remember that time we tried to do Yorkshire in a day? Absolute disaster. Drove for hours and saw nothing but rain and sheep. Speaker_1: (Laughing) Don’t remind me! Honestly, it was a complete waste of petrol. We should have just stayed in bed. Though, thinking about it, we did find a particularly nice tea room in Haworth. Speaker_3: Oh, I remember that one! Had a lovely scone with clotted cream and jam. Alright, alright, Yorkshire isn’t *all* bad. Speaker_2: Speaking of disasters, how’s Sarah doing? You said she’d been having a bit of trouble with, well, you know… Speaker_1: (Sighs) Oh, it’s a complicated one. Seems she’s decided to give young Mark another chance. I just don't understand it. He treated her terribly. But she says she’s hoping he’s changed. Honestly, women… Speaker_3: (Raises an eyebrow) Don’t start on the women now, Arthur. You’ve had your share of complicated relationships yourself, haven’t you? Speaker_1: (Grumbling) That’s different. That was a long time ago… And it’s not something I like to dwell on. Now, where did I put those photos from the trip? I took a particularly good one of that lighthouse…

Speaker_1: This is actually really good, isn’t it? You’ve outdone yourself, Chloe. Proper comfort food. Speaker_3: It is! Seriously, after a week of salads trying to be ‘good’, this is exactly what I needed. What *is* in it, though? It’s not just beef mince and tomato, is it? Speaker_2: There’s a load of Worcestershire sauce. Secret ingredient. Me mum always puts it in her chilli. Makes all the difference. Speaker_1: Oh, that’s clever. I always forget about Worcestershire sauce. It's a game changer. Right, so, anyone got any…drama to spill? My week’s been spectacularly uneventful, which is nice for once. Just spreadsheets and lukewarm coffee, the dream. Speaker_3: Oh, you say that like it’s a good thing! I thrive on drama. Though, honestly, work's been a bit hectic. We had a massive production delay because one of the suppliers, apparently, their van broke down. Full of vital components. Speaker_2: Classic. Always a van, innit? Speaker_3: Always a van! I had to stay till nine last night trying to sort it out. Honestly, sometimes I think I should’ve stuck with my original plan of becoming a florist. Less stressful. Speaker_1: A florist? I didn’t know that! You, a florist? I can’t picture it. You’d be too…efficient. You'd have perfectly organised bouquets and colour-coded flowers. Speaker_3: Probably. It’s just, the thought of sunshine and pretty things is really appealing right now. Speaking of appealing, how are things with Ben? Still going strong? Speaker_1: (Sighs) It’s…complicated. We had another conversation last night. About, you know, the future. And whether we actually *want* the same future. Speaker_2: Oh, bugger. That sounds…tense. Speaker_1: It was. He’s brilliant, honestly, he is. But he’s so…content. He loves his job, his routine, his PlayStation. And I'm, like, planning world domination and booking weekend trips to Iceland. Speaker_3: You need someone who can keep up with your energy, definitely. It's no good being with someone who dampens everything. Speaker_2: Yeah, you need ambition in a partner. Someone who's always up for a laugh and a bit of adventure, you know? Not just…settled. Don't get me wrong, settled's good eventually, but not when you're twenty-something. Speaker_1: Exactly! He just doesn’t *get* why I want to go skydiving. He thinks it's a waste of money. Speaker_3: Oh, my god. That’s a dealbreaker right there. Speaker_2: Seriously. You’ve gotta have someone who’s at least willing to watch you skydiving, even if they don’t want to jump themselves. Speaker_1: I’m starting to think you’re both right. I keep making excuses for him, saying he’s just practical, but…it’s frustrating. I feel like I’m constantly toning myself down. Speaker_3: Don’t do that. Ever. You're brilliant just the way you are. You're driven, you're funny, you'd organise the apocalypse into a neat little conference schedule. Speaker_1: (Laughs) You're sweet. Okay, maybe I’ll book that skydiving thing, just to spite him. Speaker_2: Do it! And send us a video. We’ll cheer you on. More chilli? Definitely need more chilli.

Speaker_1: Oh my god, Barcelona was *amazing*. Seriously, you would have loved it. Did you have a good weekend? You didn't mention going anywhere with… Mark? Speaker_2: It was alright, pretty chilled actually. Mark was working all weekend, sadly. Just had a proper duvet day, really. Needed it after last week, honestly. How was Barcelona though? Spill! Was it as good as you hyped it up to be? Speaker_1: Better! Honestly. The food was incredible. I ate so much tapas, I think I’ve gained about five pounds. And the architecture! Gaudí is a genius. We went to Park Güell… honestly, it was like stepping into a fairytale. Speaker_2: Ooh, Park Güell sounds incredible. I've seen pictures. Did you manage to actually, like, *relax* at all? You're always rushing around on holiday. Speaker_1: I did! A bit. We spent a whole afternoon just sitting on the beach, people-watching. And drinking sangria, obviously. It was bliss. Thinking about it makes me want to book flights back already. We should go together next year! Maybe Paris? Speaker_2: Paris would be lovely! Although, expensive. Maybe we should start saving now? How much did Barcelona actually set you back? Speaker_1: Hmm, probably around seven hundred quid, all in. Flights were reasonable, but the accommodation was a bit pricey. And I did a bit of shopping… don't tell my bank account. Anyway, enough about my spending habits. What did *you* get up to, aside from the duvet day? Did you watch anything good? Speaker_2: Not much, honestly. Watched the new series of ‘The Fall of the House of Usher’ on Netflix, that was pretty good. Dark, as you’d expect from Mike Flanagan. And I attempted to bake a cake, which was… a disaster. It’s currently residing in the bin. Speaker_1: Oh no! Baking fails are the worst. I tried making macarons once. It did *not* end well. Mum was over visiting last week and was going on about my cousin Sarah getting married next year. Apparently, it's going to be huge. Speaker_2: Oh really? Where? I haven't spoken to your aunt in ages. Speaker_1: Devon. She's always wanted a big posh wedding. Mum's already stressing about what to wear. She's asked me to be a bridesmaid, which is… a lot. Speaker_2: Oh wow. That’s a big commitment! But good, you'll have fun. Speaking of commitments, any news on the boyfriend front? Still seeing… what’s his name, Ben? Speaker_1: Ugh, Ben. We're… on a break. A very indefinite break. He’s just… a bit exhausting, you know? Constantly needing reassurance. It was draining. Speaker_2: Oh no, that’s rubbish. You deserve someone who makes you feel good, not someone you have to constantly mother. We need to have a girls’ night. Come over on Friday? We can order a takeaway and watch something terrible. Speaker_1: Yes! Absolutely. That sounds perfect. Indian? Thai? I’m craving spice after all the paella. Speaker_2: Ooh, Thai sounds good. And we can dissect Ben's failings over spring rolls. It’s a deal. And maybe… just maybe… we’ll start planning that Paris trip. Speaker_1: Amazing! Deal. And yeah, dissecting Ben is *definitely* on the agenda. Speaker_2: Good. Now, tell me again about this sangria…

Speaker_1: …and honestly, the paperwork was just relentless. Mountains of it. You’d mark thirty essays, finish feeling quite pleased with yourself, and then realise there were another fifty reports to write. It felt like the marking was just a sort of…interlude between the actual *work* of being a teacher. Speaker_2: Sounds brutal. It went down really well, initially. But scaling it up…that’s where the headaches started. Finding suitable venues, getting the licenses, insurance…it was a logistical nightmare. Speaker_1: That sounds fantastic, though! So different from my world of Year 11 English Literature. A pop-up cinema! I’d have loved to have gone. Did you ever show any Hitchcock? Speaker_2: Sometimes. *Psycho* always went down well, naturally. Though finding a venue with soundproofing for *that* was…an experience. Actually, the biggest logistical challenge wasn’t the films themselves, it was the popcorn. Seriously. Trying to get a reliable supplier for decent popcorn was a full-time job. Speaker_1: (Smiling) The popcorn! That’s brilliant. It’s always the little things, isn’t it? You spend all this time thinking about artistic vision, and then get bogged down in the practicalities of snack provisions. Speaker_2: Exactly! And people are *very* particular about their popcorn. It has to be perfectly salted, perfectly buttered…it’s a minefield. I’m glad I moved onto something a bit less…granular now. I import olive oil from Greece. Less drama. Speaker_1: Olive oil? That sounds lovely. And far more relaxing. What made you decide to make that switch? I always thought entrepreneurs were relentlessly driven, always chasing the next big thing. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Relentlessly driven to avoid stress, more like! The cinema was fun, but it was exhausting. And frankly, I realised I preferred the slower pace of building relationships with suppliers, ensuring quality…it’s a different kind of satisfaction. Plus, I get to spend a lot more time in places like this, which is a bonus. Have you always been a teacher? Speaker_1: Almost. I took a year out after university to travel, did the usual backpacking thing, and ended up working on an organic farm in Australia for a while. That was… enlightening. Covered in mud, picking fruit for minimum wage, questioning everything I thought I knew about life. But it made me realise I actually enjoyed explaining things, helping people understand things. So, I did my PGCE and never looked back. Though sometimes, on a particularly challenging Monday morning, I do briefly reminisce about the simplicity of picking mangoes. Speaker_2: (Raises his coffee cup) Here’s to mangoes…and escaping paperwork. And maybe, just maybe, finding the perfect popcorn supplier one day. Speaker_1: Cheers to that! Speaker_2: Are you back to the UK soon? Maybe i should find a cinema near you.

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m starting to think living with Chloe and Liam was a mistake. Speaker_2: Oh, not again. What’s happened now? Did Liam leave his dirty socks everywhere *again*? They’re both a bit clueless sometimes, aren’t they? But hey, at least the flat’s usually clean…ish. Speaker_1: That’s only because *I* clean! Liam just moves the mess from one corner to another, and Chloe thinks dusting involves waving a cloth vaguely in the direction of the furniture. Speaker_2: You’re exaggerating. Speaker_1: Am I? Last week, I found biscuit crumbs in the bathroom! *The bathroom,* Ben! Speaker_2: Okay, fair point. Biscuit crumbs in the bathroom is a crime against hygiene. But think about it, you need them to balance out all the tidiness. It’s… feng shui. Speaker_1: Feng shui doesn’t involve rogue digestive biscuits, Ben. And it's not just the mess. Chloe keeps borrowing my clothes without asking! I went to get my favourite jumper yesterday and it wasn’t there. Found her wearing it to the supermarket. Speaker_2: Right, that’s proper annoying. Have you said anything? Speaker_1: I tried. It just turns into a whole ‘Oh, I thought you wouldn’t mind’ and a dramatic sigh. It’s exhausting. I spend half my time feeling like their mum, not their housemate. Speaker_2: Hmm. Maybe you should have a proper sit-down chat with them? Like, lay down some ground rules? Speaker_1: I don’t want to be *that* person. The controlling housemate. But honestly, I’m starting to dread coming home sometimes. Speaker_2: You're not being controlling, you just want a bit of respect for your stuff and a bit of help around the place. It’s reasonable! And honestly, a slightly cleaner bathroom would be a blessing. Speaker_1: It would be a miracle. I just… I don’t know. Maybe we should start looking for a new place when our lease is up. Speaker_2: Whoa, hold on. Let’s not jump to that yet. Maybe a chat will make things better. We can even practice what you're gonna say in the car, if you want. I can be Chloe and you can unleash the fury. Speaker_1: (laughs) Okay, okay. Maybe that’s a good idea. But if she uses my shampoo again, all bets are off. Speaker_2: Deal. Now, quick, tell me what you’re going to say. And be dramatic. I’m ready for my role. Speaker_1: Right… “Chloe! My shampoo! The purple shampoo! Do you have *any* idea how much that costs?” Speaker_2: (in a high-pitched voice) “Oh… I just thought it smelled nice! And… my hair was really dry!” Speaker_1: (exasperated) “Dry hair is not a justification for grand theft shampoo, Chloe!” Speaker_2: Ha! You’re good at this. Speaker_1: Years of practice, living with chaotic housemates.

Speaker_1: Right then, that was a bit of a kerfuffle wasn’t it? Parking was awful. Speaker_2: Awful doesn't even begin to cover it, Arthur. I thought I’d never get a space. Ended up right at the back, near the delivery entrance. Nearly lost a wing mirror to a van. Speaker_1: You and me both, nearly took out old Mrs. Higgins’ shopping trolley trying to squeeze in. She gave me a right look, she did. Said I was a menace to society. Speaker_2: Oh, she always does. She's a character, that one. Did you manage to get the biscuits I asked for? The ginger snaps? Speaker_1: Course I did. They were on offer, two for three pound. Couldn’t resist. Figured we could have a little dunk in our tea later. Speaker_2: Lovely. And the milk? Did they have the semi-skimmed? I swear they're trying to force us all onto that fancy whole milk stuff. Speaker_1: They did, but they were nearly out. Only a pint left. Thought I'd grab it, rather than risk them not having any tomorrow. Speaker_2: Good thinking. That’ll do nicely. Oh, and did you remember to pick up that tin of peaches for Betty? She’s been craving them. Speaker_1: Oh, blast it all, no! I completely forgot Betty's peaches. I was thinking about the tomatoes for your salad and… slipped my mind. Speaker_2: Arthur! She’ll be ever so disappointed. She was looking forward to having some with her custard. Speaker_1: Oh dear. I'm terribly sorry, love. I'll pop back out tomorrow, first thing. Promise. It's not far, is it? Speaker_2: It's not the distance, Arthur, it’s the hassle. Getting there, parking… it’s a nightmare. But alright, tomorrow then. Speaker_1: Tomorrow it is. I’ll make a note. How’s your knee feeling today? Any better after the heat? Speaker_2: A little, yes. Still a bit stiff, but not throbbing like it was. I managed a little potter in the garden this afternoon. Deadheaded a few roses. Speaker_1: Good, good. Don't overdo it though. You don't want to have another flare-up. Why don’t you put your feet up now, I’ll make us a nice cup of tea with those ginger snaps? Speaker_2: That sounds perfect, dear. Just perfect. And maybe we can watch that detective programme you like on the telly? Speaker_1: Certainly can. A nice cuppa, biscuits, and a bit of Poirot… doesn’t get much better than that, does it? Speaker_2: No, it certainly doesn't. Now, let’s get this shopping put away before the kitchen floor is covered in carrier bags. Speaker_1: Right you are. Let's get to it. Speaker_2: Honestly... that car park. I don't know how we survive it sometimes. Speaker_1: We're hardened veterans of the supermarket wars, my dear. We'll survive. We always do. Speaker_2: That’s true enough. And at least we got everything… mostly. Speaker_1: Mostly is good enough for today. Mostly is very good enough indeed. Speaker_2: Shall we start unpacking, then? Speaker_1: Best be. Let’s get this done! Speaker_2: Alright. You take the tins, I’ll do the fruit and veg.

Speaker_1: Right, now then, tea’s nearly ready. You two behave yourselves for your Grandad and Gran. Don’t be winding them up too much. Speaker_2: (Muttering) I wasn’t planning on it. Speaker_3: (Chuckles) Oh, don’t you worry about him, Margaret. He's all bark and no bite, aren’t you, lad? Though he did try to convince me the other day the TV was spying on us. Speaker_4: It *is* spying on us, Elsie! They’re collecting data, I tell you! It's in the news! Speaker_1: (Sighing good-naturedly) Oh, here we go. Your Grandad's read another article on the internet. He believes everything he sees, bless him. Speaker_2: Seriously? Spying? What data would it want from us? Like, what we had for tea? Speaker_4: It's more complicated than that, lad! They know where you go, what you buy, who you talk to… Speaker_3: He thinks they’re building a robot army, Margaret. A robot army controlled by the television! Speaker_1: Honestly, it’s exhausting. Anyway, how was school today, Leo? Any dramas? Speaker_2: Not really. Maths was alright. We started on quadratic equations. Speaker_1: Oh, good. Those are the tricky ones. Honestly, marking those GCSE papers… the things kids try and write! You wouldn’t believe. Speaker_3: She’s a clever woman, our Margaret. Always was good with numbers. Remember in school, she used to correct the teachers? Speaker_1: (Blushing) Now, Mum, don't exaggerate! I just… pointed out a few errors. Speaker_4: (Snorting) Few? She practically ran the maths department! She’d have ‘em all in a state, she would. Speaker_2: Sounds scary. Speaker_1: It wasn’t scary, Dad, just… thorough. How are you both feeling? Did you have a nice journey over? Speaker_3: Lovely journey, dear. A bit bumpy on the A64, but nothing we couldn't handle. And the driver was a nice young man, very polite. Speaker_4: He was going a bit slow, though. I kept telling Elsie, I said, "Put your foot down, Elsie! We haven’t got all day!” Speaker_1: (Smiling wryly) You always were impatient, Dad. Speaker_2: Actually, I was thinking… Could we watch a film later? Maybe that new superhero one? Speaker_3: Oh, that sounds nice. I do enjoy a good film. As long as it’s not too scary, mind. I jumped a mile last time we watched that horror one. Speaker_4: Elsie’s a scaredy-cat, always has been. Unless it’s a documentary about pigeons, then she’s fearless! Speaker_3: They’re fascinating creatures, Arthur! Very intelligent. Honestly, you wouldn’t understand. Speaker_1: (Chuckles) Alright, alright, let’s not have a pigeon debate. Tea’s ready. Leo, will you get the biscuits? And Dad, please try not to start any arguments about the television's espionage capabilities. Speaker_2: (Heading to the kitchen) Biscuits coming up! Maybe I’ll hide the remote afterwards, just in case. Speaker_1: Good thinking. That might save us all a headache. Speaker_4: (Muttering under his breath) They *are* watching… I know it.

Speaker_1: Honestly, this wait is ridiculous. I’ve been scrolling through TikTok for a solid twenty minutes now. Brain is turning to mush. Speaker_2: Tell me about it. I should be replying to me nan, she sent me about fifty photos of her new cat. Seriously, fifty. Each one slightly different. Speaker_3: Fifty? Blimey.
